correctness.rationale: For the sixteen-vertex Clebsch Cayley graph on \(\mathbb F_2^4\) with connection vectors \(S=\{1,2,4,8,15\}\), the threshold-two update sets the next excited vertices to currently resting vertices with at least two excited neighbors, while the next refractory set is the current excited set. Disjoint excited/refractory masks enumerate exactly \(3^{16}\) states. Independent complete 43,046,721-state programs use (i) two-mask orbit walking with an exact A(E) table and first-repetition classification, and (ii) ternary-index complete functional graph plus indegree peeling and reverse depth propagation. Both yield precisely 361 recurrent states: one fixed and 90 length-four cycles, sharp entry time 7, identical 11 entry/period cells and individual basins 42987801, 60x644, 30x676. The 1,920-automorphism script checks all 90 cycles and two plane-geometry orbits (30 parallel and 60 twisted), with explicit sample four-cycles. All decoded code and saved output replayed; finite proof conditional on faithful execution, not an infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: A canonical highly symmetric triangle-free, five-regular strongly regular graph is a motivated small benchmark for contact-threshold excitable media. Changing threshold one to two reduces the known seven-period, 2,976,617-recurrent-state system to 361 periodic states without eliminating all oscillations. The surviving 90 waves fall into precisely two affine two-flat symmetry types whose basin sizes are different (676 versus 644), and exact full-state entry statistics show a sharp seven-update extinction cutoff. These are natural complete, non-implied finite invariants with structural geometry, not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice.
